## How they got there
Real Madrid reached the final by winning their group stage and defeating Liverpool 1-0 in the decisive match. Their profile was defined by exceptional passing volume, a high pre-season UEFA coefficient, and disciplined defending with only 7.8 fouls committed per game. These three metrics represent the areas where they outperformed the vast majority of their peers during the first phase.

## Would the model have picked them?
The model would not have selected Real Madrid for the final, as it ranked them fifth, placing them outside its top two predictions. Although the club's actual probability of reaching the final was 19.0%, this exceeds the base rate of 12.5% for a random knockout team. The model's expectation aligns with the semi-finals, indicated by an expected stage score of 2.04. This prediction was pushed upward most significantly by 66.0 attacks per game and pulled downward primarily by 8.8 long passes as a percentage of total passes.

## Weak spots
Real Madrid beat only 6% of teams in that season's first phase with their 8.8 long passes as a percentage of passes. They performed better than just 12% of the field regarding their 110.3 distance covered per game. Their defensive record saw them beat 44% of teams against 9.0 opponent shots per game.
